01 · The full set

Ways of wearing a world.

The new TKI, Merican, Lam Keng and Sund studies join Temenggong, Nine Rains and Kora from Part IV. All seven now have a detailed illustrated wardrobe sheet in one atlas.

Formal ceremony remains more enveloping. Everyday, sport and light fieldwear explore bare male chests, open layers, short aprons and divided wraps. Each sheet uses one wearer as a design study; every school welcomes every body type, ancestry and haircut.

How to read each sheet: upper row, left to right—formal ceremony, everyday, sport or movement, light field service. Lower row—everyday side and rear studies, then construction close-ups. Select a sheet to enlarge it.

The written register names the intended construction. Image-specific notes record where a generated drawing differs. All detailed designs are directions; knots, fabric performance, acoustics and equipment are proven in the workshop.

01 / Parallax
New detailed sheet in this volume

Toa Keng Institution

A frame can be inherited, adjusted and questioned.

Keep the four-button ceremonial jacket, narrow tie, silt marker and precise pocket geometry. Outside ceremony, a short open waistcoat frames the bare torso.

Oxidised tealCharcoalIvorySilt rust

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
The tailored frame and open everyday waistcoat read clearly; the ceremonial jacket shows extra buttons where the brief specifies four. The survey-cap inset illustrates a brim; the sliding mechanism comes next. Correct the button count and define the visor parts in the next drawing.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Light four-button scholar jacket, ivory shirt, narrow tie, straight trousers and a narrow offset silt sash. The small offset head planes are a headwear direction.

Everyday

Bare chest inside an open sleeveless waistcoat, tailored shorts, offset pocket and a small silt-coloured waist strip. No casual necktie or automatic undershirt.

Sport / movement

Bare chest, divided training shorts and an offset side gusset for precision footwork. Remove the tie, sash and waistcoat.

Light field service

Bare chest with a light open tool vest, secured pockets, shorts, grip footwear and a split-brim survey cap. A compact weather layer can be carried.

Read the side and rear.

Read the side cutaway and the waistcoat back as one garment. Keep the same pocket side, waist marker and short hem across front, profile and rear.

A worldbuilding tension.

Formal continuity and everyday openness can coexist. TKI can retain the disputed tie in ceremony without forcing it into every task. Its headwear geometry should remain modest enough to be worn.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Four buttons and silt cloth

Retain the institutional closure and a narrow cloth that can visibly carry wear. The ceremonial marker should not expand into an unrelated grand sash.

A weathered appearance is a visual cue for how the Straits dye ages.

Detail 02

Offset pocket

Locate the opening where a seated or reaching wearer can access it. The pocket follows an articulated seam.

Access and load-bearing need a real mock-up; the drawing does not prove either.

Detail 03

Adjustable split brim

The survey cap explores a frame that changes with the wearer’s task. Keep the band low and the moving edge legible.

The sliding mechanism and its stability are next to resolve.

Next movement study: Sit to write, reach across a work surface, turn the head under the visor, open a pocket one-handed and compare the same vest on several adult torsos.

02 / Amanah
New detailed sheet in this volume

Al-Merican College

What is valuable need not be readable by a stranger.

Keep the outside plain and the valuable cloth inward. The reveal is a deliberate gesture. A narrow functional strap may carry a ledger pouch across the otherwise bare torso.

IndigoCreamSubdued brassPlain linen

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
The outside is much quieter, and the waist close-up depicts an intentional inner reveal. The open ceremonial coat still shows a wider lining strip than the fingertip-width brief, so normal concealed wear and a deliberate reveal should be drawn as separate states. Verify the pouch and strap anchor across views; control loose waist-tie ends in sport.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Long unstructured linen coat, cream inner garment and tapered trousers; one inherited fastening and only a tiny inner edge visible. Three shallow headwrap folds remain an option.

Everyday

Bare torso, a narrow shoulder strap and small ledger pouch, plain folded-waist indigo trousers and low deck shoes. The heirloom facing stays inside the waist fold.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and secure plain divided rowing breeches. Put the pouch, strap and headwear aside; avoid trailing ties.

Light field service

Bare torso, rolled plain trousers and a low secured waist pouch for light dock custody. Footwear and added layers follow the actual job.

Read the side and rear.

Follow the narrow shoulder strap to its waist tab. The back stays bare, the pouch remains in the same position, and the inward-facing cloth stays inward.

A worldbuilding tension.

The earlier images repeatedly exposed too much patterned cloth. This family should make the difference between normal concealment and an intentional reveal especially clear.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Deliberate inner reveal

A hand turns the waist fold to introduce a small heirloom textile that normally faces inward. Give the return fold enough depth to conceal it again.

The close-up is an intentional disclosure, a moment in the day.

Detail 02

Inherited fastening

One small fastening and a well-finished inner seam can carry more meaning than abundant exterior ornament.

Ownership, repair history and the occasion of disclosure are fictional details still to develop.

Detail 03

Inside the folded headpiece

A low folded headpiece may hold an inner pocket or loop for an entrusted item. Keep the outside quiet.

A drawn pocket still needs access, comfort and retention tests.

Next movement study: Open and reclose the waist fold; sit, walk and step onto a deck; remove the pouch for training; test how the folded headpiece is accessed without dismantling it.

03 / Communion
Detailed sheet carried from Part IV

Sri Temenggong Institution

Cloth becomes a carried responsibility.

Keep the deliberate waist fold, narrow border, shoulder cloth and low leaf-folded headpiece. Ceremony can expand the cloth; ordinary life leaves the chest and much of the back open.

ForestQuiet goldWarm creamEarth

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
Carried from Part IV: the sports wrap still has a long front tail, and the border is more ornamental than intended. Shorten and secure the tail; test the tying sequence in cloth.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Roomy cream long-sleeved upper garment; full kain over ankle-length trousers; a restrained shoulder drape; low leaf-folded headpiece; removable sandals.

Everyday

Bare chest, knee-length folded kain over divided shorts, a cloth carried on one shoulder and a low tied hair band. The shoulder cloth ends visibly at the back.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and a short, securely managed hip wrap over divided shorts. No shoulder drape or trailing tie. Bare feet belong to this clean-floor footwork study.

Light field service

Bare chest, compact wrap, secured shoulder cloth and a small pouch for light stewardship. Foot and shin coverage follows the terrain and work.

Read the side and rear.

Check how the waist fold crosses the hip, how the shoulder cloth hangs down one side of the back, and whether a raised arm pulls at the waist.

A worldbuilding tension.

The earlier writing both refuses displayed rank and lets responsibility be read in the border. For this pass the readable difference becomes a temporary duty, returned afterward.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Waist fold and inner tie

The proposed overlap needs a repeatable tying sequence, enough adjustment and a way to resist loosening when sitting.

The knot’s strength is for the workshop to prove.

Detail 02

Narrow woven border

A quiet border can identify the entrusted cloth without covering the garment in ornament. Repair and wear should remain possible.

The geometric marks are invented for the Straits.

Detail 03

Leaf-fold headpiece

A modest rise comes from folded cloth. The knot, internal support and hair attachment need to be visible in a detailed pattern study.

It should fold down for storage and remain comfortable when the wearer turns.

Next movement study: Kneel, sit on the floor, step high, raise both arms, remove sandals and refold the wrap. Observe the same adult garment on different waist and hip proportions.

04 / Recomposition
New detailed sheet in this volume

Lam Keng College · 南景书院

An inherited form can disclose how it was changed.

Keep asymmetry, an edited seam and visibly different long and short proportions. A cohort marker has a defined place; it is not random ornament scattered through the outfit.

Ink charcoalCinnabar seamStoneParchment

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
The short one-shoulder everyday panel, cuff-to-hem tab study and exposed rear give this family a clearer construction identity. Some seams read as raw edges where a finished revised join is intended. Check the exact panel and tab positions across occasions, then distinguish permanent joins from removable tabs.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Fully clothed long side-split scholar coat over a long light shirt and trousers, stepped hem, one reworked older panel and a small cuff tab. Low folded headcap with unequal planes.

Everyday

Mostly bare chest and abdomen with a very short open asymmetric vest or a single shoulder panel. Divided shorts carry a stepped side panel and the cohort tab at a defined hem.

Sport / movement

Bare chest, divided athletic shorts and a short secured split side panel. Long coat tails and loose panel ends are removed for urban movement.

Light field service

Bare chest under a compact open work vest or removable shoulder piece; divided work shorts, a removable forearm piece and task-appropriate shoes.

Read the side and rear.

The small shoulder panel should occupy only the intended upper-back area. Keep much of the back bare, align joining tabs between views and preserve the same stepped hem and cohort-tab position.

A worldbuilding tension.

The twenty-year revision cycle can produce multiple historical silhouettes. This sheet studies one candidate family; it should not erase the possibility that another cohort dressed differently.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Unpicked and rejoined seam

A small cinnabar line can show where one panel was revised. The new seam performs a real join.

The illustration cannot establish seam strength or whether the old cloth remains sound.

Detail 02

A relocated cohort marker

The formal cuff and sleeveless everyday hem can carry the same marker under different location rules. Show the migration clearly.

Actual dates and a cohort chronology have not been assigned in this visual pass.

Detail 03

Reversible cap corner

A turned corner exposes a replaced lining or panel. Reversibility should be evident in the edge finish and attachment.

The cap’s folding pattern is next to draft.

Next movement study: Raise an arm, sit, bend, replace the short panel, turn the cap and compare cuff versus hem marker placement across all four occasions.

05 / Reciprocity
Detailed sheet carried from Part IV

House of Nine Rains

A garment records its use without becoming a billboard.

Keep the narrow record band, plain work cloth, contrasting repairs and repairable woven headwear. The daily torso stays open; formal dress adds the tunic and mantle.

UndyedRain indigoRepair threadPale straw

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
Carried from Part IV: the record band is broader and more decorative than the brief; the physique is idealised where the brief asked for a softer workaday build. The canopy detail suggests a join; the next drawing shows replacement.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Plain undyed tunic and loose trousers, a rectangular short mantle, narrow record band, and a shallow open-weave ceremonial canopy.

Everyday

Bare chest, narrow record band, divided work shorts, visible repairs, grippy shoes and a woven sunhat. The record must remain attached without spreading into a large sash.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and secure opaque knee-length swim shorts. Put the shoulder band, packet and hat ashore. The identifier reduces to a small waistband marking.

Light field service

Bare chest, anchored record band, reinforced shorts and a compact tool belt for light monitoring. Terrain-specific footwear is part of the task.

Read the side and rear.

Check the shoulder-to-waist route across the otherwise bare back, the exact anchor point and whether the packet swings. Keep repairs in the same locations across views.

A worldbuilding tension.

The older heavy-cotton work tunic survives as a task or ceremonial layer. The new daily direction moves durable cotton toward lower garments and tool-bearing pieces. Material weight is to be measured in wet conditions.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Band and repairable anchor

The band can join a cloth waist tab through a small loop, easy to release.

The grid is a fictional record system; its encoding has not been designed or validated.

Detail 02

Contrasting stitched patch

A repair should have a visible damaged area, a patch overlap and a stitch path that can be worked again.

Printed patch graphics and clean rectangles alone do not explain a repair.

Detail 03

Replaceable hat edge

A replaceable woven edge segment connects to the ribs through accessible lacing, so damage need not discard the whole hat.

An open canopy is not automatically waterproof. Drainage, shading and wind behaviour need physical tests.

Next movement study: Squat, reach to measure water, carry a small packet, wet and dry the band, remove and replace a hat segment, and inspect how a repair behaves after repeated movement.

06 / Third Voice
Detailed sheet carried from Part IV

Kora House

Expression can be deliberate without announcing every movement.

Keep matte softness, one exposed shoulder, quiet-looking joins and an open relationship between headwear, hair and ears. Colour remains a wearer choice; this plum family is one sample.

Soft plumSmoky roseCharcoalEarth

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
Carried from Part IV: the fastening detail shows a knot where the brief describes a cloth loop; the formal headwear stays low where a sculptural roll was imagined. Draw those alternatives separately and test cloth sound.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Long pleated wrap-coat and inner layers, sculpted soft shoulder volume, flat quiet shoes and a soft head roll that sits clear of the ears.

Everyday

Bare chest and one soft drape over one shoulder, with substantial pleated divided lower wear. The waist join should hold the cloth without creating a full poncho.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and soft pleated divided training shorts; no shoulder cloth or headwear. Bare feet are shown for the clean-floor breath-and-movement study.

Light field service

Bare chest, compact shoulder cloth tied clear, soft lower layers, cloth pockets and task-appropriate quiet footwear. Observation and mediation are the proposed roles.

Read the side and rear.

Check the exposed back, the one-sided shoulder panel, a stable waist join and ear clearance when the head turns. The garment stays the same wrap in every view.

A worldbuilding tension.

A single uniform colour or silhouette would work against the earlier freedom of colour and acoustic specification. Treat this as one approved construction family among several, subject to actual sound testing.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Head roll, ear and hair

The soft head structure can sit behind the ear while leaving room for curls or other hair forms. Attachment must not rely on one haircut.

A design option, alongside personal and religious head coverings.

Detail 02

Cloth-loop fastening

A sewn fabric loop and a short controlled tail can reduce loose hard components. The join should be reachable by the wearer.

Silence, strength and ease of dressing are proven in the fitting room.

Detail 03

Pleat and folded seam

Pleats give the lower garment movement without a long trailing layer. A folded seam can contain loose edges.

Only material samples and movement tests can establish what sound the cloth actually makes.

Next movement study: Turn the head, raise an arm, sit, gesture and walk over timber and stone. Compare cloth sound and sole sound separately, and keep deliberate audible signalling available.

07 / Commons
New detailed sheet in this volume

The Sund Commons

Care can be ceremonial without becoming opulence.

Keep deep allowances, standard fittings, accessible repairs and the wearer tab. The ordinary cap can serve ceremony after maintenance; the waist apron leaves the daily chest open.

Grey greenSlateOff whiteCharcoal

Palette.

Image inspection / retain for revision
The same plain cap, waist apron and turned hem carry the intended shared-maintenance logic without a grand ceremonial addition. The repair locations still vary between views, and the body remains more muscular and idealised than the requested softer workaday build. Fix a repair map and test the garments on a broader range of adult bodies.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Best-maintained shared lightweight jacket, plain shirt and trousers, deep hems, standard buttons and a discreet wearer tab. The same ordinary workcap is cleaned and repaired.

Everyday

Bare chest, short waist apron over substantial work shorts, usable pockets and deep hems. No chest bib, rear vest or prestige jewellery.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and work-derived athletic shorts with a replaceable reinforcement panel. The apron and cap come off for strength-and-carry practice.

Light field service

Bare chest, compact waist tool apron, secured pockets, work shorts and the ordinary three-panel cap. Separate task protection is added where needed.

Read the side and rear.

Read the waist-apron band around the otherwise bare back. It must be adjustable and reachable. Match hem depth, pocket placement and repairs across views.

A worldbuilding tension.

Sund should not acquire a grand ceremonial cape simply for visual parity. The challenge is to make the same plain garment visibly worthy of care, transfer and public use.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Standard button and spare allowance

A compatible button and generous seam allowance let the garment be repaired or altered for another wearer.

The image needs a real size and interface specification before “standard” is more than an intention.

Detail 02

Deep hem and wearer tab

The turned hem shows spare length and a small tab with several prior wearer marks. It can carry history while remaining an ordinary working detail.

No names are assigned here; the marks in the picture are not readable archive entries.

Detail 03

Repaired cap panel

An accessible stitched edge allows one cap panel to be replaced. Ceremony presents the repair with pride.

Repeated washing, fit across hair types and repair access still need material tests.

Next movement study: Transfer the garment between different adult bodies; let out a hem; replace a button; adjust the apron from behind; remove a cap panel and repair its edge.

09 · The comparative register

Seven differences
that should survive the render.

SchoolBelonging is carried byWhat to resist
TKIArticulated seam, framed torso, precise pocket, silt marker and adjustable field of view.Letting the sash or academic headpiece become a generic fantasy court costume.
MericanA deliberate inner reveal, plain exterior, functional carrying strap and inherited fastening.Displaying heirloom pattern across all outer surfaces.
TemenggongPractised waist fold, controlled shoulder cloth and a border entrusted with duty.Turning every responsibility into permanent rank or leaving sportswear unsecured.
Lam KengA revised join, unequal panels, stepped proportions and a marker placed by cohort rules.Mistaking arbitrary asymmetry or random red lines for a revision history.
Nine RainsNarrow record band, visible repair and accessible replacement parts.Inflating the band into decoration or treating the canopy as proven weather protection.
KoraIntentional soft volume, controlled joins, ear clearance and material choice.Assuming soft-looking cloth is silent or making one colour compulsory.
SundAdjustable allowances, standard fittings, the wearer tab and ordinary care.Adding ceremonial grandeur that conceals its shared construction.

Open torsos make waists, folds, pockets, shoes and headwear carry more of the identity. Each school keeps its own answer.

Where the next pass can go

Resolve construction.

Draw the changing states of a fold, fastener or removable panel. Match details across views and make a small cloth mock-up.

Broaden the wearers.

Test different adult physiques, hair volumes, genders and ways of moving without making institutional identity depend on one model.

Put them in a shared scene.

A corridor, workshop or public gathering can show how these wardrobes coexist, age, get borrowed and become street fashion.

This complete character register adds the other four detailed sheets and carries all seven families together, alongside the historical evidence and earlier draft directions.

All seven sheets were made using the built-in image-generation tool. Adult reference models and repeated views support development, but face, physique and garment details can still drift. Image-specific notes distinguish what the brief intended from what the picture actually shows.

The package contains seven original PNGs, seven same-dimension JPEG copies, both detailed-study prompt registers, development notes and this standalone HTML. The HTML embeds viewing copies and opens them in an enlarged viewer. Original dimensions are stated per image; no upscaling or verified pattern work is implied. No live website has been changed.
